title: 感恩节前空管出问题：新设备跟旧设备说不上话，出行高峰前能修好吗？
speaker: George Ferguson

segments.en: George, let me just have you parse what we heard there from the secretary talking about patches, new technology. What do you make of what happened? How holistic of an understanding do we
segments.zh: 乔治，请解读一下部长提到的补丁和新技术。你如何看待发生的情况？我们对事件的全貌了解多少？

segments.en: have of what happened to your own Friday? Well, so I think we just have a very small understanding at this point. But we know there's a large amount of legacy systems inside the US air control system
segments.zh: 周五的事我们目前了解有限。但美国航空管制系统内有大量遗留系统。

segments.en: and it's going to be very difficult to get a single fix. You're going to continue to have to lay it into an existing system so you can keep air travel going while you're improving the system.
segments.zh: 很难一次性修复。必须嵌入现有系统，在改进的同时维持航空旅行。

segments.en: It's a constant job. So I think it'll be a challenge when I hear them say that they need sort of one big 40, 50 billion dollars to upgrade it all right away. And I think these kind of problems
segments.zh: 这是持续的工作。他们说要立即投入四五百亿美元升级，我认为是个挑战。这类问题

segments.en: continue. And again, it sounds like they've laid in some new equipment that isn't communicating correctly with old equipment. I'm glad they found it before Thanksgiving weekend because it's going to
segments.zh: 会持续。听起来新设备与旧设备通信不畅。幸好感恩节周末前发现，因为届时会更忙。

segments.en: get even busier out there. So I'm kind of surprised it's breaking down here.
segments.zh: 会更繁忙。所以现在出故障，我有点意外。
